question: Does a single-layer linear-attention architecture admit a parameter setting whose forward output on a full-rank design matrix equals its ordinary-least-squares fitted values, and does that construction support a useful slow-versus-fast-memory interpretation of transformers?

key_findings.claim: For a fixed full-rank dataset, the paper gives an algebraically valid factorization of the OLS fitted-value map through its defined linear-attention block.
key_findings.evidence: With (1/n)X^T X = V Lambda V^T, it sets L = V Lambda^(-1/2), P = (1/n)L^T X^T Y, W_Q = W_K = W_V = L, W_FFN = I, and W_P = P. Because (1/n)L^T X^T X L = I, the block output reduces to XLP = X(X^T X)^(-1)X^T Y.

key_findings.claim: The construction is a per-dataset representation witness, not a transformer algorithm that computes OLS from an input dataset in one forward pass.
key_findings.evidence: The forward input in Equation 2 is X alone, while L is precomputed from the inverse square root of X's empirical covariance and the output head P is precomputed from both X and the target vector Y. Thus the covariance inversion and target cross-product required by OLS have already been placed in the parameters before the advertised forward pass.

anchors.section: 2.2 Decomposition of the coefficient vector, Equations 6-8

key_findings.claim: Under the proposed parameterization, attention does not itself discover the inverse covariance; it applies an identity in whitened coordinates and the data-dependent head supplies the remaining OLS coefficient information.
key_findings.evidence: The key inserted factor is exactly (1/n)L^T X^T X L = I. The attention term therefore returns XL, after which P maps those whitened features to fitted targets. This is useful as a factorization but does not substantiate the stronger claim that attention intrinsically solves a new OLS instance.

anchors.section: 2.2 Isomorphism to the Linear Transformer architecture, Equations 7-8

key_findings.claim: In the sole experiment, a tied one-dimensional construction approaches its analytic OLS state during optimization.
key_findings.evidence: The task is y = 2x + epsilon with n = 500 and epsilon distributed as N(0, 10^-4). The only learned scalar L starts at 0.5 and is optimized with Adam for 5,000 epochs while P is defined analytically from L, X, and Y. Figure 1 reports that training MSE and relative distance to OLS approach their floors within roughly the first 1,000 epochs and that L approaches L* = ((1/n)X^T X)^(-1/2).

key_findings.claim: The empirical result does not demonstrate that ordinary training discovers a general OLS solver.
key_findings.evidence: It optimizes one scalar on one fixed one-dimensional dataset, continually defines the output head using that dataset's X and Y, and evaluates on the same fitted values. The paper does not specify the distribution of x, learning rate, Adam parameters, seed, held-out data, final numeric errors, or uncertainty, and it tests no multivariate or rank-deficient case.

key_findings.claim: Even in the scalar experiment, the fitted output does not uniquely identify the claimed positive whitening parameter, so the plot is a selected reachability branch rather than proof of unique structural emergence.
key_findings.evidence: For k=1 and the experiment's analytically recomputed P(L), the defined block output is proportional to L^4: writing s=(1/n)X^T X and c=(1/n)X^T Y gives Output(X)=X s c L^4. Both L=+s^(-1/2) and L=-s^(-1/2) reproduce the OLS fitted values. Initialization at L_0=0.5 selects the positive branch shown in Figure 1, but no other initialization, stability test, or uniqueness argument is supplied.

key_findings.claim: The proposed slow-fast decomposition yields a clear covariance-shift distortion formula under its assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: Treating LL^T = Sigma_x^(-1) as fixed slow memory and (1/m)Z^T Y_z as context-dependent fast memory, and assuming Y_z = Z beta, gives predicted values Z[Sigma_x^(-1) Sigma_z]beta. The construction recovers Z beta only when the inference and training empirical covariances match.

anchors.section: 3 Slow and Fast Memory in OLS-Transformer, Equations 9-10

key_findings.claim: The paper's inference formula consumes the very inference-set labels it outputs, so it is not an out-of-sample prediction rule as written.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 9 requires Y_z to produce the vector of predictions for Z; there is no separate unlabeled query z_* and no construction that ingests labeled context pairs while withholding the query target. The result is a transductive fitted-value reconstruction with target access, not ordinary inference on unseen labels.

anchors.section: 3 Slow and Fast Memory in OLS-Transformer, Equations 9-10

key_findings.claim: The slow-fast 'inference' equation is not the forward pass of the OLS-Transformer defined and proved in Section 2.
key_findings.evidence: Applying Equation 2's fixed parameters to Z would produce (1/m)(ZL)(ZL)^T(ZL)P. Equation 9 instead writes (1/m)ZLL^T Z^T Y_z: it drops the learned head P and the Section-2 value path ZL, substitutes the target labels Y_z as values, and therefore changes both inputs and computation. The covariance-distortion identity in Equation 10 is algebraically valid for Equation 9, but it does not analyze the architecture whose isomorphism was proved in Equations 7-8.

key_findings.claim: The extension from the OLS construction to standard transformers is a conceptual comparison rather than a derived or tested result.
key_findings.evidence: The paper lists nonlinear activations, distinct Q/K/V projections, softmax, multiple heads, and positional encoding, then connects softmax attention to modern Hopfield energy and exponential storage. It supplies no theorem or experiment showing that these changes repair the covariance sensitivity, preserve its OLS factorization, or explain modern-LLM reasoning.

key_findings.claim: The central OLS-as-attention observation has a close, uncited predecessor from 2025.
key_findings.evidence: Ordinary Least Squares as an Attention Mechanism (arXiv:2504.09663) already rewrites OLS prediction as a restricted query-key-value attention computation in a transformed regressor space. The present paper's reference list does not include it, sharply narrowing novelty to its particular tied-L/FFN/head factorization, scalar reachability plot, and memory discussion.

method.core_idea: Whiten the columns of one fixed full-rank design matrix, tie all three linear-attention projections to that whitening matrix, and choose a data-dependent output head so the resulting product equals the OLS fitted-value projection.
method.mechanism: The paper eigendecomposes the empirical covariance (1/n)X^T X, builds its inverse-square-root factor L, and rewrites beta_hat as LP with P = (1/n)L^T X^T Y. In its attention-FFN-head product, the three tied L projections make the middle Gram factor equal the identity, leaving XLP. A one-dimensional optimization study learns scalar L while recomputing the analytic target-dependent head; in that scalar setting the output depends on L^4, so the displayed positive solution is not unique. For the memory interpretation, the paper switches to a different formula: it freezes LL^T from training as slow memory and calls a new context's label-feature cross-moment fast memory, deriving Sigma_x^(-1)Sigma_z even though that formula is not the Section-2 forward pass. It then qualitatively situates linear attention between classical Hopfield memory and softmax attention.
assumptions: X has full column rank, so X^T X is invertible and its inverse square root exists.
The complete design matrix X is known before parameters are chosen, because W_Q, W_K, and W_V all contain its empirical-covariance whitening matrix.
The complete response vector Y is known before the forward pass, because the output head P = (1/n)L^T X^T Y is target dependent.
The forward pass is evaluated on the same X used to construct L and P rather than on a distinct query design matrix.
The architecture omits softmax, residual connections, normalization, masking, nonlinear activation, bias, and conventional tokenization of labeled examples.
All Q, K, and V projections are tied to one square k-by-k matrix and the FFN is the identity.

The empirical reachability result assumes a one-dimensional linear relation, one fixed sample of size 500, Gaussian response noise of variance 10^-4, and an analytically recomputed data-dependent head.
The slow-fast derivation assumes training and inference contexts share exactly the same noiseless coefficient beta and that the inference labels Y_z are available.
The slow-fast discussion assumes Equation 9 represents the earlier OLS-Transformer even though it removes P and replaces the defined value path with Y_z.

The Hopfield discussion assumes that similarities among linear attention, quadratic associative energy, and softmax attention justify an architectural progression, although no such progression is proved here.

techniques.role: Uses an eigendecomposition to make the attention Gram factor an identity matrix.
Sets all query, key, and value projections to the same inverse-square-root covariance factor.
Encodes the label-feature cross-product needed for the OLS coefficient in the final projection.
Optimizes a single scalar toward its analytically known whitening value and compares outputs with OLS.
Separates a frozen inverse training covariance from a context-dependent feature-label cross-moment.
Expresses mismatch as the multiplicative distortion Sigma_x^(-1)Sigma_z.
Tracks whether sufficient statistics are supplied as inputs or hidden inside dataset-specific parameters.

evaluations.setting: One-dimensional y = 2x + epsilon regression with n = 500, epsilon ~ N(0, 10^-4), tied W_Q = W_K = W_V = L, identity FFN, P = (1/n)L^T X^T Y (transpose immaterial for scalar L), L initialized at 0.5, and Adam optimization for 5,000 epochs
evaluations.metric: Training MSE and relative distance between the model predictions and the analytical OLS fitted values
evaluations.result: Figure 1(a) shows both curves falling to their displayed floors, with the text reporting functional alignment within approximately the first 1,000 epochs; exact final numbers and uncertainty are not reported
evaluations.baseline: Closed-form OLS fitted values on the same 500 training samples

evaluations.setting: The same single-scalar, single-dataset optimization run
evaluations.metric: Learned L trajectory relative to L* = ((1/n)X^T X)^(-1/2)
evaluations.result: Figure 1(b) shows L rising from 0.5 to the plotted analytical target at roughly the same time as the output curves stabilize; no repeated-run statistics are provided

limitations: Author-defined scope: the theorem assumes full column rank and deliberately removes softmax and normalization layers to isolate linear operations.
Author-stated: the slow-fast formula is highly sensitive to discrepancies between training and inference covariance matrices.
Reviewer-identified: both the inverse-covariance factor and the target cross-product are computed outside the forward pass and embedded in parameters.
Reviewer-identified: the theorem establishes instance-specific representability, not one fixed transformer that solves new OLS problems in context.
Reviewer-identified: the output is fitted on the same X used to build the parameters; no unlabeled test query or conventional labeled-context token sequence is modeled.
Reviewer-identified: the inference analysis requires Y_z while purporting to predict Y_z.
Reviewer-identified: Equation 9 is not Equation 2 evaluated on Z; it drops the target-dependent head and substitutes Y_z for the proved architecture's value computation.
Reviewer-identified: the only experiment is a one-dimensional, one-sample, one-scalar optimization with no held-out set or comparator trained under the same protocol.

Reviewer-identified: because the scalar output is proportional to L^4, positive and negative whitening roots are functionally indistinguishable; one positive initialization cannot establish unique structural recovery.
Reviewer-identified: the x distribution, optimizer learning rate and other Adam settings, random seed, numerical final errors, and uncertainty are omitted.
Reviewer-identified: rank-deficient, underdetermined, noisy multivariate, regularized, and intercept-containing regression are not addressed.
Reviewer-identified: the exact prior Ordinary Least Squares as an Attention Mechanism is omitted from the references.
Reviewer-identified: claims about modern LLM reasoning, robustness, and Hopfield-capacity evolution are not established by the theorem or experiment.
failure_modes: Applying the advertised parameters to a new design matrix changes the whitening identity, so the same block no longer equals that matrix's OLS projection.
Changing labels while holding parameters fixed leaves the output unchanged because Y is not an input, contradicting the behavior required of an OLS solver across tasks.
A singular or nearly singular X^T X makes L undefined or numerically unstable without a pseudoinverse or regularization.
Using the inference-set labels to construct fast memory leaks targets and cannot predict a genuinely unseen response.
Treating Equation 9 as the same model as Equation 2 silently changes the value input and head, so conclusions about the proved OLS-Transformer's context behavior need not hold.
Covariance shift multiplies beta by Sigma_x^(-1)Sigma_z and can rotate or amplify predictions severely under ill conditioning.
A tied linear block may fit the scalar demonstration while failing under multivariate correlations, noise, intercepts, or changed sample size.
Treating a factorization as a learned algorithm can conceal that the expensive inverse and sufficient statistics were supplied externally.

Extrapolating the linear construction to softmax or multi-layer transformers can fail because the identity factorization is not preserved by normalization, residuals, nonlinearities, masking, or causal token order.
reusable_insights: Whitening converts a covariance-weighted linear-attention product into an identity, which is a compact way to expose classical projection structure.
Separate architectural representability from algorithmic execution by inventorying every data-dependent quantity hidden in weights.
A label-dependent output head is a sufficient statistic, not evidence that the preceding attention block inferred labels.
Covariance mismatch can be audited explicitly through an operator such as Sigma_train^(-1)Sigma_context rather than described only as distribution shift.
Slow-versus-fast memory is most informative when the slow component is genuinely task shared and the fast component is computed from permitted context inputs.
Analytically constrained toy optimization is useful for reachability checks, but it should be paired with task-distribution training and held-out queries before making learning-algorithm claims.
Novelty searches for algebraic equivalences should include synonymous formulations such as attention mechanisms, kernel smoothers, transformed regressor spaces, and in-context linear regression.
open_questions: Can one fixed linear or softmax transformer ingest arbitrary labeled context pairs and compute an accurate OLS or ridge prediction for an unlabeled query without externally supplied inverses?
What minimum depth, width, heads, or iterative recurrence is required to approximate a pseudoinverse uniformly over bounded condition numbers?
Does the tied-L construction retain any advantage over directly placing beta_hat in a linear output head once all preprocessing costs are charged?
Can a task-shared slow memory and label-permitted fast memory be defined so that the covariance-shift formula predicts real in-context generalization rather than fitted-value reconstruction?
How does the method behave for rank deficiency, intercepts, heteroskedastic noise, ridge penalties, multivariate outputs, and separate queries?
Would multiseed experiments across random task instances learn the analytic whitening transform without recomputing a target-dependent head each step?
Which contribution remains after a line-by-line comparison with Ordinary Least Squares as an Attention Mechanism?
Can the claimed Hopfield-energy progression and its memory-capacity consequences be stated and proved for the exact architecture used here?

competitive_landscape.title: Ordinary Least Squares as an Attention Mechanism
competitive_landscape.difference: This earlier paper already rewrites OLS predictions as a restricted query-key-value attention module in a transformed regressor space. The present paper adds a particular tied whitening-factor/identity-FFN/data-dependent-head factorization, a scalar reachability plot, and slow-fast/Hopfield commentary, but its headline OLS-attention equivalence substantially overlaps this prior result.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers as Statisticians: Provable In-Context Learning with In-Context Algorithm Selection
competitive_landscape.difference: Bai et al. construct transformers that implement least squares, ridge, Lasso, and other procedures from labeled context with near-optimal predictive guarantees and algorithm selection. This paper uses one linear layer but obtains exactness by making its projections and head specific to the same X and Y being fitted.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent
competitive_landscape.difference: Von Oswald et al. show one linear self-attention layer can realize a regression gradient step and study task-shared weights learned across regression instances. The present work contrasts this with a nominal closed-form pass, but it externally supplies the instance's inverse covariance and label statistic rather than computing them in context.

competitive_landscape.title: Trained Transformers Learn Linear Models In-Context
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. analyze gradient-flow training of a single linear self-attention layer over random regression tasks, prove convergence to a global minimum, and characterize covariate-shift brittleness. The present experiment learns one scalar for one fixed dataset and derives a related covariance mismatch without task-distribution training.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Transformers are Versatile In-Context Learners
competitive_landscape.difference: Vladymyrov et al. interpret each layer as maintaining an implicit regression weight and learn preconditioned, momentum-like algorithms under heterogeneous noise. This paper instead gives a static per-instance exact factorization and does not show a reusable learned optimizer.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers learn to implement preconditioned gradient descent for in-context learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Ahn et al. prove that global minima or critical points of linear-transformer pretraining implement one or more preconditioned gradient steps and that the preconditioner adapts to a task distribution. Here the desired preconditioner is analytically inserted from the one dataset before the forward pass.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
competitive_landscape.difference: Schlag et al. already establish formal equivalence between linearized self-attention and slow-controller/fast-weight memory updated by outer products, including capacity limitations and corrective updates. The present paper specializes a fixed/fast split to an OLS covariance factorization but does not establish a new general memory mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
competitive_landscape.difference: Ramsauer et al. prove that the modern continuous Hopfield update is equivalent to transformer attention and has exponential storage under stated conditions. The present paper offers a qualitative path from its linear OLS block to that result rather than a new capacity theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: In-context learning of closed form solution to simple linear regression task using transformer with linear self-attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Hagiwara's July 2026 follow-up constructs a linear-self-attention Transformer that approximately obtains a simple least-squares closed form in context using layer normalization and tests whether training acquires the construction under L1 regularization. It is narrower in regression dimension and only approximate, but unlike the reviewed paper it explicitly targets reusable in-context computation rather than putting the current dataset's inverse covariance and labels into fixed weights. As post-target work it does not affect April priority, but it narrows the current claim that the reviewed factorization uniquely supplies a one-pass closed-form route.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first direct structural isomorphism making OLS a special case of a single-layer Linear Transformer, plus a resulting slow-fast memory framework and an evolutionary bridge to softmax/Hopfield associative memory.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its concrete contribution is the factorization L = V Lambda^(-1/2), P = (1/n)L^T X^T Y with tied W_Q = W_K = W_V = L and an identity FFN, together with a one-scalar convergence figure and the covariance-distortion expression Sigma_x^(-1)Sigma_z. Secondary checking confirms the factorization but also shows that the scalar output is proportional to L^4 and that the slow-fast Equation 9 is not the proved forward pass.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The broad OLS-as-attention claim is not new: arXiv:2504.09663v2 states essentially that result before this paper, and several earlier in-context-learning papers already connect linear attention to least-squares algorithms. What remains potentially distinctive is the exact tied-L/identity-FFN/head presentation and its short memory narrative. Even that construction is a representation identity, not a one-pass solver for new problems, because L and P already contain the current inverse covariance and labels. The purported inference analysis then changes the architecture and reads the targets. July 2026 work further demonstrates a different, genuinely in-context approximate closed-form route for simple regression. Claims about intrinsic statistical inference, unique structural emergence, modern-LLM reasoning, and a derived Hopfield-capacity evolution should therefore be narrowed substantially.

reviewer_notes: Independent secondary verification re-read all six pages of the exact pinned arXiv:2604.13656v1 PDF and extracted text, including Equations 1-10, both rendered Figure 1 panels, every architectural and Hopfield claim, conclusion, and all references. Local PDF/text SHA-256 values were recomputed and exactly match the indexed provenance; the official arXiv record checked on 2026-08-23 still lists v1 (2026-04-15) as current. The algebra in Equations 3-8 was re-derived dimension by dimension; the audit newly records the scalar +/- whitening non-identifiability and the fact that Equation 9 changes the proved architecture while consuming Y_z. Three official-primary search families covered OLS-as-attention, linear-Transformer in-context regression/covariate shift, and the paper's special-case/one-pass novelty language. Nine current exact-version arXiv records were inspected, including the omitted pre-target near-duplicate and a July 2026 post-target closed-form competitor.
